desc.D08: Checks the data is structurally sound: missing periods, duplicate records, out-of-range values, unflagged schema changes, and whether validation checks run before each forecast
desc.D10: Checks all the data has arrived before each forecast run, and whether runs ever start on partial data
desc.D43: Checks the history the model learns from reflects true demand: stockouts recorded and lost sales corrected, returns and cancellations handled
desc.D09: Checks spikes and drops are detected, explained as real events or data errors, and treated before training
desc.D11: Checks the trend, seasonality and structural breaks in the data are understood and handled by the model
desc.D37: Checks each series has enough history, and how new or short-history items are forecast
desc.D14: Checks features use only information that would have been known at the time the forecast was made
desc.D15: Checks backtests fed drivers (price, promotions, weather) as they were known at forecast time, not as they actually turned out
desc.D12: Checks which inputs actually drive the forecast, and whether they match what the business believes drives demand
desc.D13: Checks each input earns its place: does accuracy drop when it is removed?
desc.D16: Checks for inputs that duplicate each other and add noise or instability
desc.D17: Checks whether the inputs' values are shifting over time compared with the data the model was trained on
desc.D39: Checks planners can see why a forecast changed, for example through a driver breakdown
desc.D18: Checks the model performs as well on new data as on the data it was trained and tuned on
desc.D20: Checks forecasts don't change materially between runs for reasons other than new data, such as random seeds or refits
desc.D19: Checks how model settings (or ARIMA-style orders) were chosen, and whether small changes swing the results
desc.D21: Checks model runs, settings and results are recorded, so any model can be reproduced and compared
desc.D22: Checks accuracy was tested over many past cut-off dates rather than a single train/test split
desc.D23: Measures forecast error with standard metrics, at the horizons the business uses
desc.D24: Checks for systematic over- or under-forecasting
desc.D34: Checks the model beats simple baselines such as repeating last year's value (seasonal naive)
desc.D25: Shows where errors concentrate: by product, location, period or promotion
desc.D26: Checks prediction ranges are produced and trustworthy, e.g. 90% ranges contain the actual about 90% of the time
desc.D27: Checks the remaining errors show no pattern the model has missed, such as a recurring miss around holidays
desc.D28: Checks that a claimed improvement over an alternative model is real rather than noise
desc.D35: Shows how accuracy falls the further ahead the forecast looks
desc.D36: Checks accuracy by demand type (smooth, erratic, intermittent), and whether each gets a suitable method
desc.D30: Checks production computes the inputs and runs the model the same way as when it was tested
desc.D31: Checks whether planner overrides improve or worsen the forecast
desc.D38: Checks forecasts add up consistently across levels, such as SKU, store and region
desc.D29: Checks a new or changed model was run alongside the old one before going live
desc.D32: Checks accuracy is monitored over time, and that degradation triggers action such as retraining
desc.D41: Checks forecast runs succeed on schedule, failures are caught, and fallbacks are defined and tested
desc.D33: Checks whether input data and forecast outputs are monitored for shifts
desc.D42: Not scored. Ties the findings to a root cause (model, data, inputs or process) for the recommendations
